record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: Given a chiral ring I with associated affine variety X = Spec(I), K-stability has been proposed as a criterion for when I is the chiral ring of a superconformal field theory, but known counterexamples show the picture is incomplete. What is the precise relationship between K-stability, chiral rings, and superconformal field theories?

evidence.quote: Question 15. Can we give a precise description on how K-stability is related to chiral rings and SCFTs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I$ be a finitely generated commutative graded ring over $\mathbb{C}$ (called a chiral ring) with an isolated singularity at the origin, and let $X = \mathrm{Spec}(I)$ be the associated affine variety, viewed as a (possibly Fano) cone with a chosen Reeb vector field. To such data one associates a notion of K-stability defined via test configurations and the (equivariant) Futaki invariant computed, for instance, from the Hilbert series of $I$. It has been proposed that K-stability of $(X,\xi)$ should characterize when $I$ arises as the chiral ring of a four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theory (for example, the chiral ring of a quiver gauge theory living on D3-branes probing the singularity $X$), with the Reeb vector encoding the superconformal R-symmetry obtained by $a$-maximization. However, examples are known in which the naive K-stability criterion fails to match the physical SCFT condition (e.g. when nontrivial baryonic symmetries, accidental symmetries, or further modifications of the Hilbert series numerator are required).

Problem: Formulate and prove a precise mathematical statement giving necessary and sufficient conditions, in terms of an appropriately refined notion of K-stability of the pair $(X,\xi)$ (equivalently, of the graded ring $I$ with its $\mathbb{R}$-grading), for $I$ to be realizable as the chiral ring of a four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theory. In particular, identify the correct refinement of the Futaki invariant / test-configuration framework that accounts for the known counterexamples and characterizes SCFT chiral rings exactly.
artifact.status_search_result: The precise relationship between K-stability and SCFT chiral rings remains an active research area. Foundational work (Collins–Xie–Yau) established equivalence between K-stability and existence of Ricci-flat Kähler cone metrics, and conjectured equivalence with chiral-ring stability, but recent work (e.g., 2021 JHEP "Chiral rings, Futaki invariants, plethystics, and Gröbner bases") shows that naive Hilbert-series Futaki computations must be modified (numerator corrections) to correctly diagnose SCFT chiral rings, with no complete characterization yet established. The question therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: K stability and stability of chiral ring
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes K-stability as criterion for chiral ring of SCFT; equivalence to Ricci-flat Kähler cone metric.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational conjecture relating K-stability to SCFT chiral rings.

status_evidence.title: Chiral rings, Futaki invariants, plethystics, and Gröbner bases
status_evidence.snippet: Modifies Hilbert series numerator so K-stability correctly diagnoses chiral rings; addresses counterexamples.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the relationship is incomplete and requires refinement, hence still open.
